{"id": "dda6f1d1-d655-4e2f-baad-156ad1743688", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "An Application Load Balancer (ALB) works at Layer 7 (HTTP/HTTPS/gRPC). A Network Load Balancer (NLB) works at Layer 4 (TCP/UDP/TLS).

| | **ALB** | **NLB** |
|---|---|---|
| **OSI layer** | 7 (application) | 4 (transport) |
| **Protocols** | HTTP, HTTPS, gRPC, WebSocket | TCP, UDP, TCP_UDP, TLS, QUIC passthrough |
| **Routing** | Content-based: host, path, headers, query strings, HTTP method, source IP | Connection-based: protocol and port |
| **Performance** | Scales well, with slightly higher latency because it inspects requests | Very high throughput and ultra-low latency, and it handles sudden traffic spikes |
| **IP addresses** | DNS name only, and the IPs can change | One static IP per AZ, and you can attach Elastic IPs. It also has a stable DNS name. |
| **Targets** | Instances, IPs, Lambda functions | Instances, IPs, ALBs |
| **Source IP** | Passed in the `X-Forwarded-For` header | Preserved for instance targets, and optionally via Proxy Protocol v2 |
| **Security groups** | Supported | Supported |
| **TLS** | Terminates TLS and supports SNI. It can also authenticate users through OIDC or Cognito. | Terminates TLS or passes it through to the backend |
| **Other features** | Redirects, fixed responses, weighted target groups, sticky sessions, WAF integration | PrivateLink endpoint services, cross-zone balancing (optional) |

**Choose an ALB when:**
- You run HTTP/HTTPS web apps, APIs, or microservices.
- You need path-based or host-based routing, for example `/api` to one service and `/web` to another.
- You want WAF, user authentication, or HTTP-level redirects and rewrites.
- You're fronting containers (ECS/EKS) or Lambda with rich routing rules.

**Choose an NLB when:**
- You need extreme performance or very low latency, or you expect millions of requests per second.
- You use non-HTTP protocols such as gaming, IoT, MQTT, or custom TCP/UDP.
- You need static or Elastic IPs, for example for customer firewall allow-listing.
- You're exposing a service privately through AWS PrivateLink.

A common pattern combines the two. Put an NLB in front of an ALB when you need static IPs and also want Layer 7 routing.

I can look at the load balancers in your connected AWS accounts if you'd like. I can check which type you're running, their target health, or their recent metrics.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
